title: [CEReactions] step 3 pops the element queue before invoking it; all engines invoke first

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

[[CEReactions]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#cereactions) step 3 says:

> 3. Pop the element queue from the custom element reactions stack, and invoke custom element reactions in that queue.

Read literally, the element queue is popped **before** its reactions are invoked. While those reactions run, the queue being processed is no longer the current element queue. Any reaction enqueued during the invocation therefore goes through [enqueue an element on the appropriate element queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-an-element-on-the-appropriate-element-queue): if this was the outermost [CEReactions] scope the stack is now empty, so the element is added to the **backup element queue** and a microtask is queued to process it.

A concrete case: the invocation runs an upgrade reaction for a connected element, and the upgrade enqueues that element's `connectedCallback`. The callback reaction is added to the element's own custom element reaction queue, and the element is appended to the backup element queue. The callback runs right away, because the element's reaction queue is still being drained. But the element stays on the backup element queue with an empty reaction queue, and the "processing the backup element queue" flag stays set until that microtask runs. A later reaction from a path that has no [CEReactions] scope (the parser, user editing, a native microtask) is then appended behind the stale entry. When the backup element queue is processed, the stale element's later reactions run first, so callbacks come out in the wrong order.

All three engines instead invoke the queue while it is still the current element queue, and pop it afterwards. Reactions enqueued during the invocation therefore join that same queue, never the backup queue:

- Blink: `CustomElementReactionStack::PopInvokingReactions` calls `InvokeReactions(*queue)`, then `stack_.pop_back()`.
- WebKit: `~CustomElementReactionStack` calls `m_queue.processQueue()` while `s_currentProcessingStack` is still this stack, then restores the previous one.
- Gecko: `CustomElementReactionsStack::PopAndInvokeElementQueue` calls `InvokeReactions`, then `RemoveLastElement`, with the recursion depth still set.

We hit this in an engine that followed the text literally. `html/semantics/forms/the-select-element/customizable-select/selectedcontent-custom-element-reactions.html` ("Removing the selected option ... runs the clones' reactions after remove() returns") observes the order: Chrome passes it. Switching to invoke-then-pop fixed it.

**Proposed change** to step 3:

> 3. Invoke custom element reactions in the current element queue, then pop it from the custom element reactions stack.

("Invoke custom element reactions" may need a note that the queue can grow while it is being invoked.)

Related, but not the same: #10944 and #10465.
